strategy_title: Autotuning num_warps/stages without tile changes causes regression
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune with only num_warps and num_stages variants (no BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K changes) caused a 35% slowdown. The autotuner selected a smaller block size (64 threads vs 128), which doubled register pressure per thread (128→255 registers/thread), halving theoretical occupancy from 18.75% to 9.38% and achieved occupancy from 6.25% to 3.12%. The root bottleneck (uncoalesced shared memory access from non-unit stride B-matrix loads) was not addressed because tile dimensions were unchanged, and the register spill from 255 registers/thread introduced new local load/store inefficiencies (MemoryCacheAccessPattern rule triggered at 27% speedup potential).
applicable_when: Kernel has shared memory bank conflicts (SharedMemoryConflicts rule, >10-way conflicts) and uncoalesced shared access (UncoalescedSharedAccess rule, >60% excessive wavefronts) caused by non-unit stride matrix loads; registers/thread is high (>64) limiting occupancy below 10%.
do_not_apply_when: Do not apply autotune with only num_warps/num_stages variants when the bottleneck is tile-dimension-dependent (bank conflicts from stride access patterns). Varying only num_warps without changing BLOCK sizes can cause the autotuner to select configurations with extreme register pressure (>200 regs/thread) that trigger register spilling, introducing new MemoryCacheAccessPattern bottlenecks worse than the original.
framework_notes: In Triton, @triton.autotune configs with empty dicts {} only vary num_warps and num_stages but keep all tl.constexpr tile parameters fixed. To actually change tile sizes, BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K must be promoted from body-level constexprs to kernel parameters and included in the config dicts. The key=[] argument means no re-tuning across problem sizes, which is fine for fixed-shape kernels but means the autotuner only runs once.

strategy_title: Autotune Without Tile Params Increases Register Pressure
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune with only num_warps/num_stages configs but without promoting BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K to kernel meta-parameters causes the compiler to spill more aggressively into registers (255 vs 128 registers/thread), halving theoretical occupancy from 18.75% to 9.38% and achieved occupancy from 6.25% to 3.12%. The kernel duration increased from 27.26 us to 36.35 us (33% regression) because the autotune overhead and increased register pressure outweighed any benefit from num_stages tuning. To reduce register pressure via autotune, tile sizes must be exposed as meta-parameters so the compiler can generate smaller, lower-register-pressure variants.
applicable_when: Never — this is an anti-pattern. Do not add @triton.autotune with empty config dicts (no tile size parameters) when the goal is to reduce register pressure.
do_not_apply_when: Always avoid autotune configs with empty dicts ({}) when the kernel has hardcoded constexpr tile sizes inside the body. The compiler sees multiple compilation targets with the same tile sizes but different num_warps/num_stages, which can increase register spilling without any tile-size benefit. Registers per thread went from 128 to 255, cutting occupancy in half.
framework_notes: Triton-specific: when BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K are defined as tl.constexpr inside the kernel body (not in the signature), they cannot be varied by autotune. The autotune decorator only varies parameters listed in the config dicts AND present in the kernel signature as tl.constexpr arguments. Empty config dicts {} only vary num_warps/num_stages, which can increase register pressure without reducing tile sizes.

strategy_title: Halving block size causes register explosion and occupancy collapse
strategy_description: Switching from tl.make_block_ptr with autotune (which selected block_size=64) vs the original block_size=128 caused registers per thread to jump from 128 to 252, which is near or at the hardware maximum (255). This register explosion cut theoretical occupancy in half (18.75% → 9.38%) and achieved occupancy from 6.25% to 3.12%, making the kernel 23% slower despite reducing bank conflicts. When a kernel is already register-limited (Block Limit Registers is the binding constraint), changes that increase register pressure — such as replacing scalar pointer arithmetic with tl.make_block_ptr inside a loop — will cause register spilling or explosion that worsens occupancy and throughput. The autotune configs did not include BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K variation, so the tile size stayed the same while the warp count changed, concentrating register pressure.
slow_pseudocode:
# block_size=128, 128 regs/thread, occupancy=6.25%
for k_idx in range(cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    xindex = offs_k + k_idx*BLOCK_K + stride*offs_m
    a = tl.load(A + xindex)  # scalar pointer arithmetic
    b = tl.load(B + xindex)
    acc += tl.dot(a, b)
fast_pseudocode:
# block_size=64, 252 regs/thread, occupancy=3.12% — WORSE
for k_idx in range(cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    a_ptr = tl.make_block_ptr(A, shape=(M,K), strides=(...), offsets=(pid_m*BM, k_idx*BK), block_shape=(BM,BK), order=(1,0))
    a = tl.load(a_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1))
    b_ptr = tl.make_block_ptr(B, shape=(K,N), strides=(...), offsets=(k_idx*BK, pid_n*BN), block_shape=(BK,BN), order=(0,1))
    b = tl.load(b_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1))
    acc += tl.dot(a, b)
applicable_when: Kernel has severe shared memory bank conflicts (>10-way) and occupancy is NOT register-limited (Block Limit Registers is not the binding constraint). tl.make_block_ptr is beneficial when the bottleneck is truly memory access pattern, not register file pressure.
do_not_apply_when: Kernel is already register-limited (registers_per_thread >= 128, Block Limit Registers <= Block Limit Shared Mem). In this regime, tl.make_block_ptr inside a K-loop increases register pressure dramatically (128 → 252 regs/thread), collapsing occupancy further. Also avoid when autotune configs do not vary tile sizes — without BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K in the config dict, autotune only varies num_warps/num_stages and cannot compensate for register explosion.
framework_notes: In Triton, tl.make_block_ptr used inside a loop body (rather than hoisted outside) forces the compiler to keep block pointer state in registers across loop iterations, significantly increasing register count. If block pointers must be used, hoist them outside the loop and advance with tl.advance() to minimize register pressure. The autotune configs must include tile size parameters (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K) as keys to allow the autotuner to find register-friendly configurations.
